thread:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: primary-eu1 GPU pool queue length > 12k for 4m, p95 latency > 6s, autoscaler errors observed (attach: autoscaler/primary-eu1).
sre-bot: symptoms = queue_growth, request_throttle=1.8x baseline, 503_rate rising.
tess (oncall): Acked. Paging infra-rotation. I’m taking this.
raj: Seeing high enqueue rate from hosted-api routes /v1/generate and /v1/chat. Could be a spike from a customer test. Pulling logs.
mike: I see autoscaler logs: `ProvisionFailed: quotaExceeded: requested 24 GPUs, quota 16` — autoscaler retry loop at 30s.
ingrid: Confirmed. Also API gateway is returning 502/503 on some connections as our frontends hit backend timeouts.
tess (oncall): High level plan: 1) rapid throttle at ingress for non-enterprise tenants, 2) steer a portion of traffic to west2 with relaxed cost controls, 3) try fast-eviction of idle sessions in primary-eu1 to free slots.
infra-rotation: Trying an emergency scale-up, but cloud account hit regional GPU quota hard. Opening quota ticket now.
raj: Rolling a short-term routing policy: set route weight primary-eu1 65% -> west2 35% for models with latency < 500ms requirement. Pushing policy in 30s.
deploy-bot: routing-change: policy apply succeeded (policy-id: rc-2105-01).
tess (oncall): Support, please flag any high-priority customers who require EU locality. We may bump to enterprise-only fallback.
support: Noted. Messaging prepared: "Transient increases in latency/503s in EU region; we are rerouting traffic and working on capacity. No data loss." Will post if impact expands.
mike: Dumping autoscaler excerpt: ```
I0421 12:02:03 autoscaler.go:211] ProvisionRequested: 8 gpus
E0421 12:02:33 autoscaler.go:298] ProvisionFailed: rpc error: code=ResourceExhausted desc="regionQuotaExceeded"
E0421 12:02:33 autoscaler.go:299] Retrying in 30s
```
raj: Also seeing error in allocation pipeline: `kv-cache-reserve` failing because host count limit reached, causing backpressure in the request router.
ingrid: Can we free KV cache hot prefixes? There's a config hook for prefix-ttl.
tess (oncall): Yes. Ingrid and Mike, please run the targeted cache-evictions for older prefixes (ttl=120->30) for non-P0 customers. Use this command: ```bash
redwoodctl cache eviction --pool primary-eu1 --older-than 120s --exclude-tag enterprise
```
infra-rotation: Eviction job started. Estimated freeable GPUs (via cache reclaim) ~6 slots. Monitoring.
raj: Applying ingress throttles: non-enterprise routes set to token rate limiter 0.6x. This should cut incoming rate ~40% for bursty clients.
sre-bot: Incident marker: severity=sev2, incident_id=INC-2105-PrimaryThrottleCascade.
deploy-bot: canary deploy to west2 routing increased — rolling to 100% of weighted policy. Observability: watch `eu1_to_west2_steer.rate`.
tess (oncall): Mike / Ingrid — what's the ETA for quota approval from cloud?
mike: Support ticket submitted to cloud provider; their initial response ETA 2-4h. Not helpful for immediate mitigation.
ingrid: Eviction freed ~4 slots so far. Queue trending down from 12k to 7.2k in 6m. p95 latency down to 3.4s.
raj: West2 acceptance rate looks healthy. However, some models are not available in west2 (quantized variants only). We'll fallback to lower-capacity variants which may degrade quality.
tess (oncall): Notify product: we may route non-critical traffic to quantized variants; set expectation on quality degradation.
support: Posted customer notice to status page and to active customer threads with suggested mitigations.
raj: Quick note: trigger temporary circuit-breaker for extremely long requests (>30s) to reduce tail queue pressure. Implemented.
mgmt? (not present): n/a
infra-rotation: Still seeing occasional ProvisionFailed from provider but rate much lower now. Autoscaler backoff still in place; manual scale not possible due to quota enforcement.
mike: Running an emergency handshake with our partner account to borrow 4 spare GPUs in a different project in eu-west. If approved we can attach them and reduce cross-region steer. ETA ~20m.
tess (oncall): Good. Keep the cross-region steer live until queue < 2k and p95 < 1s for 10m window.
raj: Confirming traffic split and throttle rules in place. Dashboard panels show success rate trending up.
ingrid: After manual cache eviction + throttles + routing, 503s dropped from 4.3% -> 0.9%. Still above baseline but improving.
support: No major customers reporting production outage yet; a few dev/test workloads hit 429s.
tess (oncall): Assigning follow-ups: (1) infra-rotation to continue quota escalation, (2) raj to revert steer once healthy, (3) support to update affected customers with expected timeline. Logging postmortem tag.
infra-rotation: Partner account borrow approved. Injecting 4 GPUs into primary-eu1. Reconcile with autoscaler after attach.
raj: Received new capacity signal. Reducing west2 steer to 20%. Rebalance in 45s.
deploy-bot: routing-change: policy update succeeded (policy-id: rc-2105-02).
tess (oncall): Observability check: queue down to 1.1k, p95 0.95s. Meeting threshold.
raj: Rolling back emergency throttle for non-enterprise tenants in 2m.
ingrid: Reverting prefix-ttl back to normal. Cache warming in progress.
support: Updating status: "Service recovering; routing and throttling adjustments reducing impact. Monitoring continues."
sre-bot: Incident update: actions=eviction,throttle,steer,partner-capacity,severity=degraded->mitigated.
tess (oncall): Incident stands down but leave incident bridge open for 1h for watch. Create INC ticket and postmortem template.
infra-rotation: Filing the incident ticket (INC-2105-PrimaryThrottleCascade) with logs/commands.
raj: Preliminary RCA notes to capture: sudden client spike + regional quota boundary + kv-cache hot prefixes preventing resource churn -> cascade throttle. Recommend: pre-warm policy for high-volume customers, quota buffer increases, autoscaler soft-fallback to reserve cross-region reservation earlier.
ingrid: Add action: automated cached-prefix aging for heavy pools and more aggressive hot-prefix eviction when queue > 3k.
tess (oncall): Thanks team. :thumbsup: Closing thread for now; will reopen if spike resurges.
